title: Under an integral ring map, a prime lying over a maximal ideal is maximal
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings such that $S$ is integral over $R$ (every element of $S$ is a root of a monic polynomial with coefficients in $\varphi(R)$). Let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ be a prime ideal such that $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ is a maximal ideal of $R$. Then $\mathfrak q$ is a maximal ideal of $S$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00GS (lemma-integral-over-field, line 7782) part (2), applied to the domain $S/\mathfrak q$, which is integral over the field $R/\mathfrak p$; cf. Lemma Tag 00GT (lemma-integral-no-inclusion)
